chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Milt's all-star Chicago band with Jabbo Smith and Cassino Simpson
summary: Milt describes the band assembled to cover Louis's slot at a gangster-owned club, with Simpson, Pasquall, Floyd Campbell and Tinsley.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Way ahead of his time. I just want to tell you about that band, then we can go on with this.

This band... I have a picture of this band, too, Danny, because it's (?) come on the era when you and I were in Chicago. And I can't... I have trouble about years. [MAYBE 1930-1931] But Louis was making his first big trip to make a tour. He was playing in this club in Chicago, which I can't call the name of, and they wanted to bring in another trumpet player to cover. And as you said, the hottest trumpet player around was Jabbo....
...and he was up in Milwaukee. So they sent for Jabbo to come in from Milwaukee to take the job, and
they organized a band in Chicago. So they had Cassino Simpson...
Yeah, an all-star band. Cassino Simpson on piano... Almost, because I was in it, and I sure was no star!
It had Cassino Simpson on piano, and Scoville Browne on saxophone, they had Jerome Pasquall on saxophone. They had John Thomas. Do you remember John Thomas, the trombone player, in Chicago?
They had a drummer named Floyd Campbell. Do you remember Floyd Campbell, Danny?
A lot of personality. Very dark, good-looking man.
A very good looking man. He was something else. Well-dressed, always smiling, he had... [INAUDIBLE SENTENCE]

He had a nice voice, too. So Floyd Campbell on drums. Othello Tinsley, Paducah Tinsley from Paducah, Kentucky, who was on banjo. And I was on bass. And I tell you, that was (?)some band(?). And Cassino Simpson was

making arrangements.
And this is where I really heard Jabbo, man. He came in there, and man, I tell you, he took that place... Gangsters owned the place. It was a race horse bookie during the daytime, and it was a nightclub at night. So we didn't start until 11 o'clock at night. And Jabbo was at his height. Good-lookin' man. He was so sharp, it hurt, man. He wore them black ascot ties, and all of the ladies in town were after him, and he loved it.
